name: com.aquedra/run
title: Aquedra Run
description: Pay-per-call GIS tools for AI agents: coordinates, measurement, reprojection, elevation, terrain.

tools.name: convert_coordinates
tools.description: Converts up to 1,000 points between decimal degrees (dd), degrees-minutes-seconds (dms) and UTM, and returns each point in the requested output formats, in the input order. To change the coordinate reference system of a GeoJSON use reproject_geojson. Takes up to 1,000 points per call (WGS84 latitude and longitude, or UTM zone, hemisphere, easting and northing). Costs US$0.001 per unit (up to 1,000 points) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. Set dry_run to true to get the price without charging and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that would cost more; for heavier inputs set max_seconds from 4 to 30, where each second over the 3 included costs US$0.0005, the full time is held up front and the unused part refunded, and the price and the time used are charged if the call runs out of time or memory, or is cancelled while running.

from.description: Format of the input points: dd (decimal degrees), dms (degrees-minutes-seconds text) or utm.

to.description: Output formats to return for every point (1 to 3 of dd, dms, utm).

anyOf.description: Latitude then longitude as degrees-minutes-seconds text, e.g. 33°26'56"S 70°40'09"W (separated by a space, comma or semicolon).

points.description: Up to 1000 points. Each is {lat, lon} for dd, a text for dms, or {zone, hemisphere, easting, northing} for utm, matching `from`.

dry_run.description: When true, return the price (cost_usd) and units of this call without running it or charging anything.

max_cost_usd.description: The most this call may cost, in USD, as a number or decimal text with at most 6 decimals (e.g. 0.01 or "0.01"). A call that would cost more is refused with 402 max_cost_exceeded and nothing is charged.

max_seconds.description: Compute time limit in seconds, 1 to 30 (default 3; 1 to 3 all use the standard 3 s). The price includes 3 s of compute. From 4 to 30 (extended time) the call runs on a separate lane, where buffer accepts larger inputs, and each second over 3 costs the geo_compute_second price: the price plus all those seconds is held at the start (that is what dry_run reports and max_cost_usd is compared with), the seconds not used are refunded, and the response adds compute_ms and max_seconds. With extended time the price and the time used are charged if the call runs out of time or memory, or is cancelled while running: 422 operation_too_complex keeps the whole hold, 422 operation_too_large or 413 result_too_large (a result over 8 MiB) or 499 cancelled keep the price and the seconds used, and those errors carry cost_usd. Any other failure is refunded in full. For the elevation operations (elevation, profile and terrain), running out of time is 503 terrain_unavailable, refunded in full on both lanes, never 422 operation_too_complex.

inputSchema.description: Convert points between decimal degrees, degrees-minutes-seconds and UTM.

tools.name: measure_geojson

To change the CRS use reproject_geojson, and to buffer, simplify or clean the geometry use transform_geojson. Takes a GeoJSON of up to 50,000 features and 200,000 vertices in WGS84 longitude and latitude, and up to 1 MiB of arguments. Costs US$0.001 per unit (up to 1,000 features and 10,000 vertices) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. Set dry_run to true to get the price without charging and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that would cost more; for heavier inputs set max_seconds from 4 to 30, where each second over the 3 included costs US$0.0005, the full time is held up front and the unused part refunded, and the price and the time used are charged if the call runs out of time or memory, or is cancelled while running.

tools.name: reproject_geojson
tools.description: Reprojects every coordinate of a GeoJSON from one CRS to another (EPSG:4326, 3857, 4674, 5361, 32718, 32719 or a WGS84 UTM zone) and returns the GeoJSON. To convert individual points to degrees-minutes-seconds or UTM text use convert_coordinates, and to read a CSV, KML, GPX or Shapefile use convert_geo_file. Takes a GeoJSON of up to 50,000 features and 200,000 vertices, and up to 1 MiB of arguments. Costs US$0.001 per unit (up to 1,000 features and 10,000 vertices) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. tools.name: transform_geojson

tools.name: get_elevation
tools.description: Returns the elevation at each point, interpolated bilinearly from Copernicus DEM, a surface model (DSM) whose heights include buildings and trees, in metres above EGM2008, with each point's source and the result's dem and attribution. For elevations along a line use elevation_profile, and for the slope and elevation statistics of an area use analyze_terrain. Takes up to 1,000 points (WGS84 lat and lon) per call, within up to 16 DEM blocks (about 120 x 120 km near the equator; each 90 m GLO-90 block counts as 4). Costs US$0.002 per unit (up to 256 points) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. Set dry_run to true to get the price without charging and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that would cost more; for heavier inputs set max_seconds from 4 to 30, where each second over the 3 included costs US$0.0005, the full time is held up front and the unused part refunded, and running out of time is 503 terrain_unavailable, refunded in full on both lanes, never 422 operation_too_complex.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180), WGS84.

points.description: 1 to 1,000 points as {lat, lon}; more is 413 payload_too_large. The points of one call may need at most 16 DEM blocks of 1024 x 1024 pixels (about 30 km across at 30 m; each 90 m GLO-90 block counts as 4).

tools.name: elevation_profile
tools.description: Returns the elevation profile of a GeoJSON LineString from Copernicus DEM, a surface model (DSM) whose heights include buildings and trees, in metres above EGM2008: samples with their distance from the start and elevation, the minimum, maximum, ascent and descent, with each sample's source and the result's dem and attribution. For the elevation of separate points use get_elevation, and for the slope and elevation statistics of an area use analyze_terrain. Takes a line of up to 100 km and 10,000 vertices, up to 1,000 samples (samples or step_m), within up to 16 DEM blocks (about 120 x 120 km near the equator; each 90 m GLO-90 block counts as 4). Costs US$0.002 per unit (up to 256 samples) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. Set dry_run to true to get the price without charging and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that would cost more; for heavier inputs set max_seconds from 4 to 30, where each second over the 3 included costs US$0.0005, the full time is held up front and the unused part refunded, and running out of time is 503 terrain_unavailable, refunded in full on both lanes, never 422 operation_too_complex.

step_m.description: Distance in metres between samples, from the start, plus the end (1 to 100,000); at most 1,000 samples. Do not combine with samples. Without either, a sample every 30 m, or 1,000 samples over the whole line when that would be more.

tools.name: analyze_terrain
tools.description: Returns the area and surface area, elevation statistics, slope and aspect of a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon from the pixels of Copernicus DEM, a surface model (DSM) whose heights include buildings and trees, in metres above EGM2008 inside it, with the result's dem and attribution. For the elevation of points use get_elevation, and along a line use elevation_profile. Takes a polygon of up to 100 km² and 10,000 vertices, within up to 16 DEM blocks (about 120 x 120 km near the equator; each 90 m GLO-90 block counts as 4) and a bounding box of up to 4,194,304 DEM pixels. Costs US$0.002 per unit (up to 4 km² of polygon area) from prepaid credits; with the default 3 s it is charged only when it succeeds, and invalid input is never charged. Set dry_run to true to get the price without charging and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that would cost more; for heavier inputs set max_seconds from 4 to 30, where each second over the 3 included costs US$0.0005, the full time is held up front and the unused part refunded, and running out of time is 503 terrain_unavailable, refunded in full on both lanes, never 422 operation_too_complex.

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Answers a chat with open models on Aquedra Run's own GPUs: qwen3-8b (reasons before answering, and those tokens count as output and use up max_tokens, so set max_tokens to at least 1024); qwen2.5-3b (small text model for simple tasks); qwen2.5-coder-7b (code); qwen2.5-vl-7b (reads data: images). It runs only on idle GPUs: if the GPUs are busy the call fails with gpu_busy and retry_after_seconds, and nothing is charged. Limits are 8192 tokens of context, up to 2048 output tokens (a larger max_tokens is lowered to that, and the result then has max_tokens_requested) and 1 MiB of arguments, with no tools, JSON mode or embeddings; qwen2.5-vl-7b takes up to 2 inline data: images of up to 512 KB each, which together must fit in the 1 MiB. Costs per million tokens (input/output): qwen3-8b US$0.18/US$0.70, qwen2.5-3b US$0.05/US$0.10, qwen2.5-coder-7b US$0.025/US$0.05, qwen2.5-vl-7b US$0.18/US$0.69; minimum US$0.0005 per call, taken from prepaid credits and charged only when the call works; prompts and answers are not stored. Set dry_run to true to get the maximum a call can cost and max_cost_usd to refuse a call that could cost more.

dry_run.description: When true, return the most this call can cost (cost_usd, the hold) and the max_tokens it assumes, without running it or charging anything.

max_cost_usd.description: The most this call may cost, in USD, as a number or decimal text with at most 6 decimals (e.g. 0.01 or "0.01"). A call that would cost more is refused with 402 max_cost_exceeded and nothing is charged.

model.description: Model id, default qwen3-8b. See GET /v1/models for the ones on sale.

role.description: Who wrote the message. The tool role is not supported.

oneOf.description: An inline image as a data:image/png|jpeg|webp;base64 URL (qwen2.5-vl-7b only, up to 2 images of 512 KB each, which together must fit in the 1 MiB request).

content.description: The message text, or a list of text and image parts.

max_tokens.description: Most tokens to generate, default 1024. A larger value than the output cap (max_output_tokens in GET /v1/models) is lowered to it, and the response says so in max_tokens and max_tokens_requested. qwen3-8b's reasoning counts toward it: send at least 1024.

max_completion_tokens.description: Same as max_tokens; wins when both are sent.

stop.description: Up to 4 stop sequences of up to 64 characters each.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Read the account's credit balance (balance_usd, in US dollars as decimal text), its level (trial or paid) and limits, whether the one-time trial credits were granted, whether credit purchases are open, and the most recent credit movements.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Buy a pack of Aquedra Run credits (US$5, US$20, US$50, US$100; 1 credit = US$1), only when the user asked for it or authorized their wallet to spend. With method "card" the result has a checkout_url the person completes in their browser; this tool never charges a card. With method "usdc" and no payment, the result is an x402 payment request (isError, PaymentRequired in structuredContent); an x402 wallet pays by calling this tool again with the same arguments and the signed payment in params._meta["x402/payment"], and the result's _meta["x402/payment-response"] carries the settlement. If a result says a payment is pending, do not pay again: call again with the same payment.

pack_usd.description: Credit pack in US dollars; 1 credit = US$1.

method.description: card returns a checkout_url the person pays in their browser; usdc pays over x402.
